title: Reassigned to Kilo control and never team leader again

tellings.quote: never went back to no Wimer control they sent me to kilo control
After a few weeks, I was removed from November Control and reassigned to Kilo Control near Sturgis, South Dakota.
I remained at Kilo Command, working with a different guy, Sgt. --- -------, as a SAT team member, then leader, and then FSC.

plain: After his 1977 encounter at a South Dakota missile site, the Air Force security guard Mario Woods says he was quietly moved away from his post, and he never returned. He tells Michels he "never went back" to his old control post and was sent to Kilo Control, another missile command post in the field around Ellsworth Air Force Base. In a later telling the story is that he was never made a team leader again. His earlier written account, published by the journalist Robert Hastings on 10 September 2017, confirms the move: "After a few weeks, I was removed from November Control and reassigned to Kilo Control near Sturgis, South Dakota." But the same text goes on to say he served there "as a SAT team member, then leader, and then FSC", a SAT being a security alert team and an FSC a Flight Security Controller, the guard in charge at a post. So on the move itself the two versions agree. On his career afterward, the 2017 text says he led a team again and was then promoted, which is not what the later telling says. Woods tells it because a sudden transfer would suggest the Air Force wanted him away from what happened.

discussion.by: Former USAF Missile Security Policeman Tells of Apparent UFO Abduction at ICBM Site
discussion.text: In the account Woods wrote for Hastings in 2017 he was "reassigned to Kilo Control near Sturgis" "after a few weeks" and served there "as a SAT team member, then leader, and then FSC". The later telling says he was never made team leader again; the 2017 text says he led a team again at Kilo and then became the Flight Security Controller.
